Subject: ZenPay: DPA intake & GDPR role split — post-demo recap

Hi Lauren — great to meet the team today, really appreciate the clear timelines. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks:

Summary of ask from ZenPay call:
- You requested our DPA and confirmation on which SCC module you'd prefer (controller/processor mapping).
- ZenPay clarified you will be the data controller of customer payment data; need Redwood to confirm processor responsibilities for model inference and logs.
- You also asked for SOC 2 Type II evidence and a note on HIPAA (possible PHI in rare payment metadata).
- Requested we start the vendor security questionnaire so legal can triage while contracting moves forward.

What I can do this week:
1) Share our standard DPA template (attached) and flag the clauses you typically redline. (attachment: redwood_dpa_template_v3.docx)
2) Send a short recommendation on SCC module choice based on your controller assertion — initial read: Module 2 (processor-focused) is likely appropriate, with an explicit clause for permitted processing and subprocessor list.
3) Provide SOC 2 Type II redacted report for 2025 and our SOC point of contact. (attachment: SOC2_TypeII_2025_redacted.pdf)
4) Kick off the security questionnaire as requested — please confirm primary legal contact if different from this thread. (attachment stub: zenpay_vendor_questionnaire.xlsx)

Open questions for you: 
- Can you confirm ZenPay’s legal contact and their preferred addressing of SCCs (do you prefer an EU module mapping or the SCC 'module-based' contract we sent earlier)?
- Is there any expected PHI in payloads or will payment metadata be strictly card/transaction identifiers (we want to confirm HIPAA scoping).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today/Tomorrow: I’ll upload the DPA and SOC2 to the shared drive and add the questionnaire link.
- By Fri (7/3): Redwood to propose SCC module wording and a short controller/processor responsibilities matrix.
- Week of 7/6: Legal teams to start redline; we can route through DocuSign if you prefer a signature path.

If that works, I’ll send the shared links and DocuSign draft after this note. Thanks again — enjoyed the demo discussion.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Subject: Re: ZenPay: DPA intake & GDPR role split — post-demo recap

Thanks Monica — yes that summary is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming: ZenPay is the data controller for customer transaction records and related identifiers. We will expect Redwood to be the processor for inference and storage of short-lived logs.
- PHI: There is a non-zero chance that some merchant messages could include patient names in free-text memos; our compliance team flagged HIPAA as a conditional requirement. We will scope further, but please include a HIPAA statement in the DPA if possible.
- SOC 2: Please provide the most recent report (redacted is fine).

Legal contact: Lauren O'Neill (me) will handle initial redlines; I will loop in ZenPay Legal (legal@zenpay.com) for final review.

Questionnaire: we'll fill the vendor questionnaire but please populate any sections you can to speed review (especially data flows and subprocessor list).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — can you mark items that would typically require enterprise SLA exceptions (eg, backup retention, log access windows)?

— Lauren
Chief Privacy Officer | ZenPay
lauren.oneill@zenpay.com | +1 (617) 555-2210

Lauren — thanks for the confirmation. Per internal sync, here is our suggested path forward so your legal/compliance teams have a clear lane:

1) Controller/Processor mapping: Redwood will be processor for inference, caching, and short-lived logs. We propose an SCC Module 2-based approach with explicit permitted processing and a subprocessor appendix. If you prefer EU-specific module mapping instead, we can adapt — please confirm.

2) DPA & HIPAA: Attached is the DPA template with an optional HIPAA addendum section. If ZenPay wants the HIPAA clauses active, we can attach them and move through redlines; otherwise keep as optional addendum. (attachment: redwood_dpa_template_v3.docx)

3) SOC 2: Uploaded redacted SOC 2 Type II (2025) to the shared drive here: https://drive.google.com/zenpay/dpa-evidence

4) Security questionnaire: Ben has pre-filled the vendor questionnaire; Lauren, please review and add any ZenPay-specific notes. Questionnaire link/attachment: zenpay_vendor_questionnaire_filled_draft.xlsx (attachment).

5) DocuSign: When you confirm module preference and HIPAA addendum choice, I’ll route a DocuSign draft to legal@zenpay.com. Preview link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ZP-DPA-2026

If that aligns with your timelines, let’s target legal redline kickoff next week (week of 7/6). Happy to set a short 30-min sync between legal teams if that helps speed things up.

Thanks — Monica
